name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.eq_zero_of_isCompactOperator_image
title: An irreducible CAR representation has no nonzero compact image

content.display_title: An irreducible CAR representation has no nonzero compact image
content.one_sentence_role: Simplicity and infinite dimensionality rule out compact operators coming from nonzero CAR elements.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra: the norm completion of the increasing union of $A_n=M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under the unital embeddings $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$ (with the fixed coordinate reindexing). Write $\iota_n:A_n\to A$ for the canonical isometric inclusion and $e_{ij}^{(n)}=\iota_n(E_{ij})$ for its matrix units. A representation is a unital complex star homomorphism into the bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space. Irreducibility means nonzero action and no proper nonzero closed reducing subspace. Let $\pi:A\to B(H)$ be irreducible on a complex Hilbert space $H$. If $a\in A$ and $\pi(a)$ is compact, then $a=0$. In particular $\pi(A)\cap\mathcal K(H)=\{0\}$.
content.assumptions: The representation is unital and irreducible in the nonzero, closed-reducing-subspace sense. The space $H$ is complete. Compactness is assumed only for the represented operator $\pi(a)$.
content.conclusion: No nonzero element of $A$ can act compactly in this representation. Faithfulness makes the vanishing conclusion a statement about $a$ itself, not merely about its image.
content.proof_summary: Simplicity makes the nonzero unital representation faithful. The preimage of the compact operators is a closed two-sided ideal of $A$. If it were all of $A$, the identity on $H$ would be compact; this would make $H$, and then the faithfully represented algebra $A$, finite-dimensional. That contradicts infinite dimensionality of the CAR limit.

proof_steps.text: The exact result `representation_injective` gives injectivity of $\pi$ from simplicity and the nonzero irreducible action.
Let $J=\{x\in A:\pi(x)\text{ is compact}\}$. Compact operators form a norm-closed two-sided ideal in $B(H)$, and the representation is continuous, so $J$ is a norm-closed two-sided ideal in $A$.

Simplicity yields $J=\{0\}$ or $J=A$. In the second case $\pi(1)=I_H$ is compact, so $H$ is finite-dimensional. Injectivity then embeds $A$ linearly in the finite-dimensional space $B(H)$, a contradiction. Therefore $J=\{0\}$ and $a=0$.

content.lean_realization_notes: This does not say that $B(H)$ has no compact operators. It describes the intersection of its compact ideal with the represented CAR algebra. Infinite dimensionality of $A$ is a proved property of the fixed CAR limit, not an extra assumption on an arbitrary algebra.
